content: Every new beginning comes from some other beginning's end.
author: Seneca
sourceWork: De Vita Beata (On the Happy Life)
story:
This insight touches directly on the messy reality of human nature. Thinking about doing something gives us a comfortable dopamine hit of progress without any of the actual friction. We often use over-researching and planning as socially acceptable disguises for fear of starting.

In Seneca's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. Clarity follows action; it does not precede it. You cannot think your way into a new way of living—you have to act your way into a new way of understanding. The smallest real-world step beats the most brilliant theory.
reflectionPrompt: In what area of your life are you overthinking the ideal approach instead of taking the simple, honorable action?
